issues.body:
bench/parse carries its own [workspace] table, so neither `cargo clippy --workspace` nor the workspace nextest archive ever reaches it (ci.yml:1217 states this explicitly for the sibling bench/dict). That is precisely why bench/parse was left pinned to hdt 0.4 while crates/sparq-hdt moved to 0.7 — the harness stopped building and nothing failed. This PR fixes the current instance but leaves the detection gap open: the next sparq-hdt dependency bump can re-break the benchmark oracle the same way, and it will again only surface when someone tries to run the harness.

bench/dict already has the pattern for this (ci.yml, 'bench/dict standalone selftest (clippy + invariant checks)'), so the precedent and the cost profile (debug build, warm rust-cache) are established.
issues.fix_hint:
Add a step alongside the existing bench/dict lane in .github/workflows/ci.yml:

      - name: bench/parse standalone build (dep-drift gate)
        run: cargo clippy --manifest-path bench/parse/Cargo.toml --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings

`--locked` is the load-bearing flag — it catches both the manifest/lock drift and the two-versions-of-hdt resolution failure this PR is fixing. If wiring CI is out of scope for a dependency-alignment PR, file it as a bead/self-improvement issue rather than dropping it.
issues.title: No CI lane compiles bench/parse, so this dependency drift broke silently and can regress again

issues.body:
The PR's stated rationale is to keep the benchmark on the same upstream release as sparq-hdt. bench/parse still pins `bzip2 = "0.4"` while crates/sparq-hdt pins `bzip2 = "0.6"`, so `cargo build` in bench/parse compiles both (observed: `bzip2 v0.6.1` and `bzip2 v0.4.4` in the same build).

This is NOT a correctness problem today: bench-hdt-zip only uses bzip2 to author the `.bz2` fixture and then hands raw bytes to `sparq_hdt::load_reader` (main.rs:1105-1126), so no bzip2 type ever crosses the crate boundary — unlike the `hdt::Hdt` value that did. It is a build-time duplication and a latent divergence between the compressor writing the fixture and the decompressor under test.
issues.fix_hint: Bump to `bzip2 = "0.6"` in bench/parse/Cargo.toml to match crates/sparq-hdt, re-run `cargo check --locked --all-targets` in bench/parse to refresh the lock, and smoke `bench-hdt-zip` on a generated fixture to confirm the `.bz2` round-trip still decodes. Purely optional for this PR.
issues.title: bzip2 stays at 0.4 while the crate under test (sparq-hdt) is on 0.6 — same class of divergence this PR is closing

verdict.summary:
Two-line dependency realignment in the standalone bench/parse harness (own [workspace] table, so zero production/workspace impact) plus the regenerated Cargo.lock. It moves the benchmark's upstream HDT oracle from `hdt 0.4 (sophia)` to `hdt 0.7 (default-features=false, features=["nt"])`, exactly matching crates/sparq-hdt's own dependency + dev-dependency pins.

This fixes a real break, not a cosmetic bump: sparq-hdt already depends on hdt 0.7, so with bench pinned at 0.4 the graph resolved two semver-incompatible `hdt` crates and `sparq_hdt::graph_from_hdt(&upstream_hdt)` (main.rs:905, :982, :992, :1095) could not type-check; the old lock also contained only hdt 0.4.0, i.e. it was stale against sparq-hdt's manifest. The `nt` feature is what `gen_hdt` needs for `Hdt::read_nt` (main.rs:872), and `Hdt::write`/`Hdt::read` remain available on the lean read path.

Verified empirically at the PR head:
- `cargo check --all-targets` in bench/parse: clean, single unified `hdt v0.7.3`.
- `cargo check --locked --all-targets`: clean and the working tree stays clean, so the committed Cargo.lock is consistent with the manifests (no drift, all new entries are registry+crates.io with checksums).
- Smoke ran the real path: `gen 200` -> `gen-hdt` -> `bench-hdt`. The archive builds via the nt writer and the correctness gate in bench_hdt (main.rs:903-909, direct vs upstream triple-count and distinct-term asserts) passes on 1592 triples. Those asserts are non-vacuous — they compare two independently-decoded graphs and panic before printing any number.

Lock churn is entirely the expected consequence: sophia/rio/sucds and their duplicate digest/sha2/generic-array stacks drop out; qwt/ahash/hashbrown 0.14/oxttl and hdt's wasm- and bin-only transitives (wasm-bindgen, clap, env_logger) come in. All bench-only; sparq-hdt already carries hdt 0.7 in the production graph, so the shipped dependency surface is unchanged.
